rationale: C16 is a clear material drafting template. The child retains its annual-observance structure, congressional-resolution recital, principal call for observance, cooperation with the President's Committee, and an unusually detailed second appeal almost verbatim, changing mainly the year, date, and the stated purpose of cooperation. C17 and C15 are also strong members of the same drafting lineage, but their operative language and participant lists are less nearly identical to the child than C16's.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 11, 1945 (59 Stat. 530), has designated the first week in October of each year as National Employ the Physically Handicapped Week and has requested the President to issue a suitable proclamation each year
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 11, 1945 (59 Stat. 530), has designated the first week in October of each year as National Employ the Physically Handicapped Week and has requested the President to issue a suitable proclamation each year
shared_material.explanation: The statutory recital is reproduced verbatim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do call upon the people of our Nation to observe the week beginning October 1, 1961, as National Employ the Physically Handicapped Week, and to cooperate with the President's Committee on Employment of the Physically Handicapped in furthering equality of opportunity for employment of the physically handicapped
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do call upon the people of our Nation to observe the week beginning October 2, 1960, as National Employ the Physically Handicapped Week, and to cooperate with the President's Committee on Employment of the Physically Handicapped in carrying out the program for employment of the handicapped
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves the complete operative framework, updating the date and adapting only the final statement of purpose.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also urge the Governors of States, mayors of cities, and other public officials, as well as leaders of industry, educational and religious groups, labor, civic, veterans', agricultural, women's, scientific, professional, and fraternal organizations, and all other interested organizations and individuals, including the handicapped themselves, to participate actively in this observance.
